label: verification

reasoning.text: The spec is a physical floorplan/visualization manifest (positions, sizes, materials, and a connection graph of named blocks), not a functional or RTL specification, so virtually every detail needed to rebuild the same behavior — modulus, widths, the conflict-free mapping equation that is the design's whole point, Barrett constants, pipeline latencies, twiddle schedule, FSM, and port/handshake protocols — had to be invented. Both engineers fell back to the same external priors (q=12289, N=1024, generic Barrett) yet still diverged on the address mapping, pipeline depths, and decimation type, confirming none of it is recoverable from the spec alone. It identifies what blocks exist and roughly how they wire together, but not what any of them computes.
gaps: [param] Exact NTT-friendly modulus q (bit-true value, not just '14-bit')
[param] Transform length N and number of stages log2(N)
[control] Conflict-free bank-index and intra-bank address generation equations
[operation] Barrett reduction parameters: mu, shift k, and number of correction subtractions
[width] Coefficient width, intermediate product width, and post-reduction output range
[operation] Butterfly decimation type (DIT vs DIF) and twiddle-multiply ordering relative to add/sub
[control] Radix-2 vs radix-4 datapath reconfiguration (lane gating, retiming) and config-selector field encoding
[timing] Pipeline latency of each stage (DSP mult, adder, subtractor, both Barrett members, register) and total core latency/throughput
[param] Twiddle ROM depth, contents/ordering, and the one-factor-fanout reuse schedule across 8 lanes
[operation] INTT N^-1 mod q constant and exactly where/when it is applied; forward-vs-inverse twiddle table selection
[dtype] BRAM organization: port width x depth, single/dual-port, read+write timing per cycle
[port] Module port lists, clock/reset polarity, and streaming handshake protocol (valid/ready vs start/done, AXI?) including FIFO widths/depths
